key_insight: Synthetic biomedical data is increasingly useful for training machine learning models, but success in simulation does not always translate to real-world performance. The paper highlights the simulation-to-reality gap as the key obstacle to turning virtual experiments into trustworthy biomedical insight.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the challenge that models trained or evaluated on synthetic data may look strong in simulation yet fail on real biomedical data, limiting their practical value and reliability.
method: Reviews the role of synthetic datasets in biomedical machine learning and explains where they help most.
Examines the simulation-to-reality gap, focusing on why synthetic benchmarks can overestimate real-world performance.
Frames synthetic data as a tool for virtual experimentation while emphasizing the need for careful validation against real data.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this paper is a reminder that synthetic data should be used strategically, not as a drop-in replacement for real data. It helps teams design more realistic evaluation pipelines and build biomedical models that are more likely to generalize in practice.

paper_title: From virtual experiments to biomedical insight with synthetic data
paper_authors: Margarida Victoriano, Milena Pavlović, Geir Kjetil Sandve, Hélder P. Oliveira, Artur Rocha
